title: Spin the Dominant Voice
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article tackles the common meeting problem of one team member dominating discussion and crowding out others. Common fixes - interrupting, private conversations, or round-robin turn-taking - tend to be short-lived or awkward, so the piece proposes a specific facilitation technique: taking the dominant speaker's own point and redirecting it back to the group for reaction, rather than shutting them down directly. It offers several scripted phrases leaders can use to execute this 'spin move,' arguing that redirecting rather than confronting preserves the dominant person's dignity while reopening space for quieter voices to contribute.
points: A dominant voice in meetings causes others to disengage and withhold contributions.

The recommended technique: take the dominant speaker's point and redirect it back to the group.

quotes: A dominant voice during a team discussion often inhibits others from making a contribution
Team members look to the leader to recapture the discussion and release the chokehold of the dominant voice.
Interrupting or talking over the energizer bunny only delays them for few moments
The maneuver employed by master facilitators is to redirect the dominant party’s contribution toward the group.
Taking something said and redirecting it allows others to take the floor.
Good leaders simply can’t allow any voice to overwhelm team discussion or drown out other voices.
